target_node: Johns Hopkins Hospital Department of Surgery
notes: route: 12_governance_societies Dean DeWitt Lewis succeeded William Stewart Halsted as professor of surgery and surgeon-in-chief at Johns Hopkins, serving until his retirement in 1939. He is the second of the department's chairs and closes the post-Halsted leadership gap between Halsted (d. September 1922) and Alfred Blalock (from 1941). Governance bar satisfied: documented surgeon-in-chief / professor-of-surgery appointment, not an administrative dean/VC title. Corroborating locator: the Johns Hopkins Department of Surgery history page, which names the post-Halsted chair succession as Lewis, Blalock, Zuidema, Cameron, Freischlag, Higgins. Independent corroboration: Hoopes JE, 'Letter from America: Hopkins reunion,' J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg (S1748-6815(09)00803-1), which names the first three chairmen of surgery at Hopkins as Halsted, Dean Lewis and Alfred Blalock. Tenure dates verified 2026-07-25 against the Alan Mason Chesney Medical Archives portrait record for Dean DeWitt Lewis (the evidence_locator), which states that Johns Hopkins recruited Lewis to succeed William S. Halsted as professor of surgery and surgeon-in-chief and that he held the post until his retirement in 1939; the 1925 start is consistent with the record's account of his 1925 departure from Rush. No upstream training edge is authored: Lewis took his MD at Rush (1899) and studied anatomy at Leipzig under Spalteholz, an anatomist rather than a surgical program director, so no endpoint satisfies the direct_training bar. Lewis therefore enters the person-to-person lineage projection as a trunk root.
